name: guile
desc: GNU Ubiquitous Intelligent Language for Extensions
why: GNU's Scheme implementation with a long history as an embeddable extension language, worth exploring though not obscure.

brief.what_it_is: Guile is GNU's implementation of the Scheme programming language, with an efficient compiler and virtual machine. It can run standalone Scheme programs or be embedded in C and C++ applications as an extension language. It supports the Revised5 and most of the Revised6 Scheme reports plus many SRFIs, and ships a module library that includes an HTTP server and client, XML parsing, and object-oriented programming. The homepage's examples show scripts that print text, print the date using an SRFI-19 module, and serve a plain-text response over HTTP on port 8080.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says Guile is designed to help programmers build applications that users or other programmers can extend with plug-ins, modules, or scripts. It calls itself the GNU Ubiquitous Intelligent Language for Extensions and the official extension language of the GNU project.
brief.how_it_works: Guile compiles Scheme to bytecode for its virtual machine. The homepage says its parsing and compiling tools are exposed as part of the standard module set, so new source languages can be added without writing C. Compiler front-ends already exist for ECMAScript and Emacs Lisp, with Lua support described as underway.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not describe installation. The Homebrew caveats say that after installing, you can place Guile libraries under $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/guile/site/3.0 (source), $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/guile/3.0/site-ccache (compiled), and $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/guile/3.0/extensions (extensions). They recommend adding these to your shell profile: export GUILE_LOAD_PATH="$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/guile/site/3.0", export GUILE_LOAD_COMPILED_PATH="$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/guile/3.0/site-ccache", and export GUILE_SYSTEM_EXTENSIONS_PATH="$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/lib/guile/3.0/extensions". The Homebrew formula installs guile, guild, guile-config, guile-snarf, and guile-tools.
brief.standout: Guile is a general-purpose Scheme that is also designed to be embedded, and it can host other languages. Its ECMAScript and Emacs Lisp front-ends are built on the same parsing and compiling tools it exposes to module authors. The homepage also presents it as a way for end users to share features as scripts instead of patches.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists GNU Guile 3.0.11 released December 1, 2025, a bug-fix release with some new features. Earlier releases are 3.0.10 (June 24, 2024) and 3.0.9 (January 25, 2023). I did not check the repository commit history.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not mention a license. It describes Lua support as underway, not finished. The examples are Scheme and do not cover embedding in C. The Homebrew formula's install paths and environment variables are specific to the 3.0 series. The scout note mentions a long history, which I did not verify beyond the GNU project affiliation.
quotes: Guile is designed to help programmers create flexible applications that can be extended by users or other programmers with plug-ins, modules, or scripts.
Guile is the GNU Ubiquitous Intelligent Language for Extensions, and the official extension language of the GNU project.
Guile empowers users with "practical software freedom"
